I am an old man here in Mangochi, and I have been growing beans and other legumes on this small piece of land for many years. I do not have money to buy the chemical fertilizer from the shop, and anyway beans give back goodness to the soil on their own, so I only use the manure from my goats and a little from the kraal. I plant the seed I saved from last season, the same local seed my people have always used, and because I intercrop with maize and pigeon pea, my wife and children help me weed two or three times. The rains from the lake side are enough for us, so I do not irrigate, and I cannot afford to hire people — only when planting if a neighbor comes to help we share labor.
